title: Use benchmarks to locate gaps, then train outside them
summary: Benchmark playlists are strongest as assessment tools. Once they reveal the weak category, most improvement volume should move into fundamentals and weakness-specific training blocks.
why: Benchmarks tell you where the hole is, but repeating the same assessment tasks is usually not enough to fill it.
Training tends to transfer better when the benchmark result leads to a separate improvement block.
actions: Keep benchmark runs for measurement, then spend the main block on fundamentals or weakness-specific tasks.
After a benchmark exposes a weak category, choose one supporting routine for that category and run it consistently for several sessions.
Retest the benchmark after the block instead of checking progress every few runs.
avoid: Do not let benchmark reruns consume most of your improvement time.

drills.label: Weakness block after benchmark
drills.reason: A dedicated follow-up block turns benchmark feedback into training instead of endless retesting.

evidence.claim: Benchmarks should point the player toward fundamentals and targeted routines instead of acting as the full routine by themselves.
evidence.excerpt: Voltaic frames benchmarks as a starting point for finding weaknesses and then selecting routines.
